message.content:
**Paris Get‑away Planner** *(Assuming a 7‑day trip, mid‑budget, and a mix of classic sights + hidden gems)* | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|---------| | **Day 1 – Arrival & Orientation** | • Arrive at Charles de Gaulle or Orly.
• Take RER B to Gare du Nord → Metro Line 4 to **Châtelet‑Les Halles** (central hub).
• Check into a boutique hotel or Airbnb in the 2nd/3rd arrondissement (e.g., Hotel Le Six, Hôtel Henriette). | • Walk to **Louvre Museum** (open 9 am–6 pm).
• Grab a quick lunch at **Café Marly** overlooking the pyramid. | • Dinner at **Le Coupe Chou** (classic French, cozy).
• Night stroll along the Seine, cross the Pont des Arts. | | **Day 2 – Classic Icons** | • Early breakfast at **Café de Flore** (Saint‑Germain‑des‑Près).
• Visit **Notre‑Dame** (exterior only, interior closed for restoration). | • Walk to **Sainte‑Chapelle** (stunning stained glass).
• Lunch at **Le Petit Cler** (market‑style bistro). | • Explore **Latin Quarter** cafés.
• Dinner at **Le Procope** (oldest café). | | **Day 3 – Art & Culture** | • Breakfast at **Ladurée** on Champs‑Élysées.
• Visit **Musée d’Orsay** (Impressionist masterpieces). | • Lunch at **Café Campana** (inside Musée d’Orsay).
• Stroll through **Tuileries Garden** → **Place de la Concorde**. | • Attend a show at **Opéra Garnier** (or a jazz club like **Le Caveau de la Huchette**). | | **Day 4 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur** | • Breakfast at **Le Pain Quotidien** near Sacré‑Coeur.
• Climb to **Basilique du Sacré‑Coeur**; panoramic view of Paris. | • Explore **Place du Tertre** (artists’ square).
• Lunch at **La Maison Rose**. | • Sunset at **Moulin Rouge** (optional cabaret).
• Dinner at **Le Coq Rico** (chicken specialties). | | **Day 5 – Day Trip** | • Take a train to **Versailles** (RER C).
• Tour the **Palace & Gardens** (book skip‑the‑line tickets). | • Picnic lunch in the gardens (pick up baguette, cheese, wine). | • Return to Paris.
• Light dinner at **L’Avant‑Garde** (modern French). | | **Day 6 – Hidden Gems** | • Breakfast at **Du Pain et des Idées** (croissants).
• Visit **Musée Rodin** (beautiful sculpture garden). | • Walk to **Canal Saint‑Martin**; lunch at **Le Comptoir Général** (vintage vibe). | • Explore **Le Marais** nightlife.
• Dinner at **L’As du Fallafel** (for a casual bite). | | **Day 7 – Shopping & Departure** | • Brunch at **Café Charlot** (classic Parisian).
• Last‑minute shopping on **Rue de Rivoli** & **Galeries Lafayette**. | • Pack & check‑out. | • Head to airport via RER B or taxi. | --- ### Practical Tips | Category | Recommendation | |----------|----------------| | **Transport** | • Buy a **Paris Visite** pass (zones 1‑3) for unlimited metro/RER.
• Consider a **Navigo Week Pass** if staying >5 days. | | **Accommodation** | • 2‑3 star boutique hotels or Airbnbs in 2nd/3rd/4th arrondissements.
• Look for free Wi‑Fi, breakfast included. | | **Dining** | • Reserve tables 1–2 hrs in advance for popular spots.
• Try **bouchons** in Lyon‑style restaurants for hearty meals. | | **Tickets** | • Pre‑book Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, and Versailles online.
• Use the official museum apps for audio guides. | | **Language** | • Basic French phrases help: “Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Où est…?”.
• Many locals speak English in tourist areas. | | **Safety** | • Keep valuables in a money belt.
• Beware of pickpockets near major attractions. | | **Weather** | • Pack layers; Paris can be cool in spring/fall.
• Umbrella handy—rain is frequent. | --- ### Budget Snapshot (per person) | Item | Approx. Cost (€) | |------|------------------| | Flights (round‑trip) | 300–600 | | Accommodation (7 nights) | 700–1,200 | | Food & drinks | 350–500 | | Transport (airport + city) | 50–80 | | Attractions & tours | 150–250 | | Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | 100–150 | | **Total** | **≈ 1,650 – 2,830** | *(Prices vary by season, booking time, and personal preferences.)* --- ### Packing Checklist - Comfortable walking shoes (Paris streets are cobblestone). - Light jacket, scarf, umbrella. - Power adapter (Type E/F). - Reusable water bottle (many cafés offer refill). - Small daypack for daily essentials. Enjoy your Paris adventure! If you’d like a more tailored plan (e.g., specific dates, budget constraints, dietary restrictions), just let me know.
message.reasoning: The user says "Plan me a trip to Paris". They want a travel plan. We can provide itinerary, suggestions, etc. There's no request for sorting. So we don't need to call the function. Just produce a plan. Provide details: duration, places, activities, budget, transport, accommodation, dining, tips. Should be helpful.
